definitions.explanation: Something that happens or takes place. Can refer to both positive and negative events, from everyday occurrences to significant incidents.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}あった{出来事|できごと}を{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Please tell me about what happened today.

examples.japanese: あの{出来事|できごと}は{一生|いっしょう}{忘|わす}れられない。
examples.english: I will never forget that incident for the rest of my life.

examples.japanese: {予想外|よそうがい}の{出来事|できごと}に{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised by the unexpected event.

notes:
USAGE: {出来事|できごと} is a neutral term for events or occurrences. It can be used for anything from daily happenings to major incidents.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{大|おお}きな{出来事|できごと} (big event)
・{小|ちい}さな{出来事|できごと} (small incident)
・{日常|にちじょう}の{出来事|できごと} (everyday occurrences)
・{歴史的|れきしてき}な{出来事|できごと} (historical event)
・{思|おも}いがけない{出来事|できごと} (unexpected event)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{事件|じけん} - incident, case (often negative, newsworthy)
・{事故|じこ} - accident
・イベント - event (often planned, loanword)
・{催|もよお}し - event, function (organized)
・{行事|ぎょうじ} - event, function (scheduled/traditional)
